note: Ceilings for scripts/bundle-budget.mjs. Measured on 2026-08-03, then rounded up
for headroom: a budget that fails on every unrelated commit is one somebody
raises without reading. Moving a number here is allowed and is the point — it
has to happen in the same commit as the growth, with the reason in the message.
What they were when they were set:
eager graph            683.5 KB   33 files
everything shipped    5500.6 KB  173 files
largest eager chunk    216.2 KB   the main route
eagerBytes moved on 2026-08-13, from 750 KB to 781 KB: the second palette
and the theme gate cost 4.4 KB, and the graph had grown to 747 KB in the
meantime, so it no longer fitted. The 30 KB of new headroom is deliberate:
at 3 KB spare, the ceiling was failing the next commit whatever it was.
The gap between the first two is what the lazy imports are worth: 4.8 MB the
window does not fetch before it can paint, most of it the PDF worker. That is
the measurement those imports never had attached to them.
The eager ceiling moved three times. To 774000, when the palette started
asking `search.query` about what is being typed: the palette is drawn by the
layout and cannot be lazy, so its ranking, its debounced query and the hits
it turns into rows are 3.8 KB the window fetches before it paints. To 784240,
for the keybinding table and its parser, which the dispatcher reads on the
first keystroke and so cannot be deferred either. Then to 794480, for the
reply bar a waiting thread offers: it exists so a blocked terminal can be
answered in one tap, and a chunk fetched on the tap is the one thing that
would take that away. Then to 800624, for the turn list a thread keeps and
the checkpoint calls behind it, which the thread panel reads on open. Then to
808816, for the mark saying an agent is driving a browser pane and the
handler answering its page questions: the mark rides on the pane's own
content, so both are read wherever a pane is drawn, before first paint.
Then to 826368, for the filing rule behind pin, settle and snooze, plus the
pinned section and the clock that wakes it: the sidebar decides where every
row belongs before it draws one. Measured at 800.9 KB, so this leaves 6.1 KB.
Then to 838656, for the environment registry and its supervisor: a window
that can hold several boites at once decides which ones to dial before it
draws anything, so the state machine and the projection cache are both on
the boot path. Measured at 812.9 KB, so this leaves 6.1 KB.
Then to 845824, for the light palette and the theme that follows the OS:
both palettes and the matchMedia watcher are applied before the first paint,
or the window opens dark and flips. Then to 851968, for the client half of
the socket-ticket exchange that replaced the shared token: a ticket is
bought before anything is drawn. Measured at 824.4 KB, so this leaves
7.6 KB. Then to 862208, for the delegation pile on the sidebar and the
detach entry beside it: +page loads the sidebar before first paint.
Measured at 835.6 KB, so this leaves 6.4 KB. Then to 870400, for the
conduct api on both backends and the orchestrator settings: the settings
store hydrates on boot and the status engine writes the pulse from its
sweep, so neither can be lazy. Measured at 844.4 KB, so this leaves 6 KB.
Then to 880640, for the dispatch device half: the layout mounts the queue
watcher and every terminal registers its sink before first paint, or a line
queued during boot finds no device. Measured at 852.4 KB, 7.6 KB spare.
Then to 890880, for the CLI manager types, i18n and catalogue row: the
settings store hydrates on boot and the shortcut bar reads the presets,
so neither can be lazy. Measured at 863.3 KB, so this leaves 6.7 KB.
largestEagerChunkBytes moved with it, 256000 -> 262144. The main route is
the chunk in question and it had 0.2 KB left, which is a ceiling that fails
the next commit whatever the next commit is.
